text:
alex: quick flag from the mamba-v1 int4 bring-up. noticed that regional indicator flag emoji (e.g., 🇺🇸 U+1F1FA U+1F1F8) in source text are getting split into separate letters or removed in the quant canary outputs. causes noisy diffs in our multilingual subtitle/translation slices (bleu ~1.1 drop on en->zh samples containing flags).

ben: can you paste a tiny repro? want to check whether the tokenizer or postprocess is to blame.

alex: repro below (utf8-aware terminal). fp16 baseline preserves the flag, int4 canary output splits into two separate regional indicator letters or sometimes drops one.

```
# repro snippet (literal bytes)
echo -n "Visit us: \uD83C\uDDFA\uD83C\uDDF8 today" | ./infer --model mamba-v1 --quant int4 --input -
# output-int4: Visit us: U S today
# output-fp16: Visit us: 🇺🇸 today
```

chen: i ran our tokenizer binary on the same input and token ids are identical pre-inference for fp16 and int4 runs. so it's likely post-gen handling.

anya: interesting. does the runtime serialize the token stream differently for quant canaries? maybe an older postproc or detok image is being used. which images are the canaries using?

dmitri: checked the canary manifests: int4 canary is pinned to `postproc:2024-06-emoji-compat` whereas the fp16 baseline uses `postproc:main`. the compat image has a small compatibility shim that calls into a C library variant that decomposes emoji flag sequences to ASCII regional letters for legacy downstream systems.

ben: that matches. i dumped the runtime's serialized token stream before postproc: both runs contained the flag codepoints intact. the transformation happens inside the postproc image.

alex: whew. at least not a quant kernel bug. still high impact for locale-sensitive samples. plan suggestion: (1) hotfix compat postproc to not decompose regional indicators by default; (2) patch the int4 canary manifest to point to `postproc:main` until compat fix lands; (3) add a regression test for regional-indicator sequences to the detok/postproc unit tests and include flags in the multilingual dev bundle.

anya: +1. also add a check in the quant bring-up checklist to validate that postproc image used by canary preserves emoji sequences that are marked as "preserve" in our locale policy.

eng-runtime-bot: [deploy] mamba-v1-int4-canary -> patching postproc image to redwood/postproc:main :gear:

ben: quick local experiment bypassing postproc (naive join) returns the emoji flag intact and BLEU returns to baseline (0.02 delta). confirms postproc is the culprit.

ci-bot: [CI] postproc PR #1102 started  added unit test for regional indicators

chen: PR adds a unit test ensuring U+1F1E6..U+1F1FF pairs are preserved and not decomposed into ASCII regional letters unless an explicit compatibility flag is set. tagging infra to add a manifest lint so future quant canaries can't accidentally use compat images with the old behavior.

ci-bot: [CI] postproc PR #1102 passed  14 tests :white_check_mark:

alex: re-ran the mamba int4 smoke after pointing to postproc:main  flag preserved, BLEU delta down to 0.03. thanks all.

anya: follow-ups: (a) add emoji flag samples (and a couple of composite emoji sequences) to the multilingual dev bundle; (b) add manifest lint in infra to assert postproc tags used by quant canaries include the emoji-preserve capability; (c) note in the onboarding doc that emoji/flag sequences are locale-sensitive artifacts to validate during bring-up.

ben: thanks team, good triage. i'll add the lint ticket and follow up on the postproc compatibility flags. :thumbsup:
